title: M_{x,0+}\B(M)_d ↔ K_{x,0+}\(K_x B(M))_d bijection
body_html:
$M_{x,0+}$ vs.\ $K_{x,0+}$ orbits on facets of $\mathcal{B}(M)$

Fix a vertex $x \in A \subseteq \mathcal{B}(M)$. Let $\mathcal{B}(M)_d$ denote the $d$-dimensional facets of $\mathcal{B}(M)$, and $K_x \mathcal{B}(M)_d \subseteq \BSigma_d$ the set of $K_x$-translates.

Lemma. The natural map $$M_{x, 0+} \backslash \mathcal{B}(M)_d > \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; > K_{x, 0+} \backslash (K_x \mathcal{B}(M))_d$$ is a bijection.
proof_html:
(option (B) — mock-exp isolated)

Surjectivity (uses (K4) only)

Any element of $K_x \mathcal{B}(M)_d$ is $k \cdot \mathcal{F}$ for some $k \in K_x$, $\mathcal{F} \in \mathcal{B}(M)_d$.

By the Levi splitting consequence of (K4) ([[node:depth_zero_reduction.K4_hypothesis]] + standard inclusion $M_x \subseteq K_x$): $K_x = K_{x, 0+} \cdot M_x$. Write $k = k_+ \cdot m$ with $k_+ \in K_{x, 0+}$, $m \in M_x$. Then $$k \cdot \mathcal{F} = k_+ \cdot (m \cdot \mathcal{F}), \quad m \cdot \mathcal{F} \in M_x \mathcal{B}(M)_d \subseteq \mathcal{B}(M)_d,$$ so the $K_{x, 0+}$-orbit of $k \cdot \mathcal{F}$ contains a facet of $\mathcal{B}(M)_d$.

Well-definedness

The map sends an $M_{x, 0+}$-orbit $[\mathcal{F}]_M$ to the $K_{x, 0+}$-orbit $[\mathcal{F}]_K$ of the same facet (using $M_{x, 0+} \subseteq K_{x, 0+}$ from (K4) and $M_{x, 0+} \subseteq M_x \subseteq K_x$). Well-defined since $M_{x, 0+} \subseteq K_{x, 0+}$.

Injectivity (this is exactly (O))

Suppose $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{F}' \in \mathcal{B}(M)_d$ have the same $K_{x, 0+}$-orbit in $K_x \mathcal{B}(M)_d$: $\mathcal{F}' = k \cdot \mathcal{F}$ for some $k \in K_{x, 0+}$. Hypothesis (O) ([[node:depth_zero_reduction.O_hypothesis]]) gives $m \in M_{x, 0+}$ with $\mathcal{F}' = m \cdot \mathcal{F}$, so $\mathcal{F}, \mathcal{F}'$ have the same $M_{x, 0+}$-orbit in $\mathcal{B}(M)_d$. $\square$

Where mock-exp enters (now isolated)

In the present formulation, the only place mock-exp enters is in the verification of Hypothesis (O), which lives outside the abstract framework. Specifically:

  • Classical setting: Cayley transform on $\mathfrak{gl}_F(V)$ $[$Stevens:SC App A$]$ + Galois descent verifies (O).
  • Tame setting: $\exp$ on $\mathfrak{m}^\perp_{x, 0+}$ (large $p$)
  • parabolic Bruhat + Galois verifies (O)
    $[$Adler, §1.5$]$.

This is the cleanest separation: the cartesian-cosheaf framework of Cartesian cosheaves Cosh^cart_G(X,R,φ) and unit isomorphism (and the §13.1 Res functor it feeds) consumes (O) as a black box, and each application provides a per-case proof.

Comparison with the old Sheaf7-era proof

The original Sheaf7 §8.1 proof embedded mock-exp directly in the injectivity step: it used the decomposition $K_{x, 0+} = M_{x, 0+} \cdot \varphi(\mathfrak{k}^\perp_{x, 0+})$ plus the uniqueness of $\varphi$ at the cell $\mathcal{F}$. This required Sheaf7 Appendix A (a 5-page development of mock-exp).

The option-(B) rewrite (2026-05-25) packages exactly this substantive content into Hypothesis (O) and applies (O) directly, without invoking the underlying $\varphi$ structure. The verifications of (O) in applications still use mock-exp, so no mathematical content is lost — just relocated for cleaner exposition.

Downstream uses

This bijection is the geometric input that allows i_x: C_d(B(Σ),𝒱)_x ≅ C_d(B(M),𝒲)_x to identify the chain complexes on $\BSigma$ and $\mathcal{B}(M)$ after taking $\kappa_x^*$-twisted coinvariants.

See also

  • [[node:depth_zero_reduction.O_hypothesis]] — Hypothesis (O).
  • [[node:depth_zero_reduction.K4_hypothesis]] — Hypothesis (K4)
  • the Levi-splitting consequence used in surjectivity.
  • Good mock exponential map and factorization M × m^⊥_{x,0+} → MG_{x,0+} — the mock-exp construction used to verify (O) in classical / tame.
